claim: A million-token model is not created by changing one context-length setting. Qwen2.5-1M combines progressive long-context training, positional extrapolation and an inference system that avoids performing every attention operation densely.

claim:
- **Train to 256K, extrapolate beyond it.** Length extension and Dual Chunk Attention play different roles; the reported million-token capability is not a million-token training curriculum.
- **Sparse prefill must respect chunking.** Attention patterns are selected from the current chunk's available queries, not from future queries at the end of the entire prompt.
- **Sparse attention does not eliminate memory.** Chunking reduces temporary activation pressure, while the model still retains a long KV history.

claim: The dense causal decoder retains the Qwen2.5 7B architecture: grouped-query attention, RoPE, pre-RMSNorm residual blocks, SwiGLU FFNs and an untied output head. The main changes concern long-context learning and attention/position handling, not a new vision encoder or expert network. Inputs are text; document retrieval and other tools are outside the decoder.

claim: RoPE normally rotates queries and keys according to their positions, so an attention pair depends on their relative distance. Distances far beyond training can become unfamiliar. DCA remaps the positional relationships to ranges the model has learned while preserving useful local continuity.

claim: In [Figure 1](#figure-1), intra-chunk attention follows ordinary local positions. Successive-chunk treatment preserves a short neighborhood across the chunk boundary, avoiding an artificial huge jump between adjacent tokens. Distant chunks use bounded/repeated positional patterns. The selected artifact supplies a 262,144-token chunk and an 8,192-token local window.

claim: Two different historical keys can receive similar remapped positional relationships. DCA is therefore an extrapolation compromise, not exact preservation of all million-token absolute distances. It also does not compress the KV cache: a remapped key still occupies a retained history position.

claim: MInference's Vertical-Slash patterns combine important key columns with diagonal bands. A small set of query rows estimates which positions matter, and offline profiling assigns head-specific pattern budgets. Dense scoring for all query/key pairs is replaced by selected patterns during the expensive prefill.

claim: The naive selection procedure examines queries near the end of the complete input. A chunked runtime cannot use those future queries while processing an earlier chunk. Qwen2.5-1M instead selects patterns using the last 64 queries of each 32K prefill chunk. This is a systems constraint on information availability, not just a smaller batch.

claim: [Figure 2](#figure-2) explains why the original pattern selector must be adapted. DCA also changes apparent positional relationships. The selection step uses continuous relative positions so distant chunks are not confused by repeated DCA patterns; the final attention computation still uses DCA positions. Selector coordinates and model attention coordinates are different contracts.
